Subject: URSA AI — Dedicated GPU pool: MAP + regional/burst decisions

Kimberly / Monica —

Following our demo earlier, URSA wants to lock a Mutual Action Plan (MAP) for dedicated capacity. They need decisions on regional placement, baseline pool size, and burst/autoscale policy so we can finalize the SOW and procurement timeline. Quick ask list below — can each of you confirm by EOD tomorrow?

Attachments: URSA_MAP_v1.xlsx, network_requirements.pdf

Ask summary:
- Regions: customer prefers us-west + eu-central; need confirmation on multi-region failover and whether we recommend a warm-failover pool or cross-region burst.
- Baseline pool sizing: URSA asked for 8x A100-equivalent GPUs to start with 2x burstable nodes for peak. Provide suggested floor and burst cap.
- Autoscale/burst policy: target P95 latency 120ms, but willing to accept short burst-based latency degradation. Need concrete burst rules (max burst concurrency, pre-warming windows).
- Security/compliance: procurement asked about SOC 2 evidence and KMS options — cc'ing Priya to help scope.
- Timeline: URSA wants to close procurement by 12/15; they want a go-live window in January.

Proposed next step: quick 30-min alignment call Fri (12/03) to finalize MAP items and hand off to implementation.

Ben

Subject: Re: URSA AI — Dedicated GPU pool: MAP + regional/burst decisions

Thanks Ben — noted. Quick internal response so we can get a clean MAP to Alex.

Decisions / recommendations (draft):
- Regions: us-west primary (closest to URSA infra) + eu-central warm standby (replicated model images, cold KV cache). Failover plan: automated DNS failover + traffic steering; we will NOT keep a hot-active cross-region pool due to cost.
- Baseline pool: start with 6 A100-equivalent GPUs in us-west. Reserve 2 GPU-equivalents in eu-central (warm).
- Burst policy: allow up to 3x baseline short-term bursts for up to 10 minutes per occurrence, with a cooldown of 30 minutes. Burst cap: 18 GPU-equivalents total across region before we throttle / fall back to smaller model variant. Ops will pre-warm cache 10 minutes before scheduled high-impact windows.
- Latency target: maintain P95 <= 120ms in baseline; during burst allow P95 up to 300ms but ensure 99th stays under 1s with graceful fallback to the smaller model.
- Security/KMS: KMS integration supported (customer-managed KMS via AWS KMS). Priya — can you confirm the SOC2 artifact checklist and runbook entries we need to provide?

I will prepare a one-page MAP doc with the above and a short decision log. For engineering handoff, I suggest Monica own the implementation runbook and assign an ops lead.

If that looks good, Ben can send this to Alex + procurement and we lock the SOW wording.
